Renati Descartes — Regulae ad directionem ingenii — Regula I
AT (Adam & Tannery) vol. X, p. 360, lines 5–14
Witness locator: AT X 360 lines 5–14
Edition: AT-X-1964 (Adam & Tannery, 1964 CNRS reprint)
==============================================================================

REGULA I.

Scientiarum finis est prudentia, quatenus non modo intellectus, sed etiam
voluntatis, ab actionibus particularibus deflectatur; atque in iis quae
sibi subiicit conditiones rationum respectu quantumvis differentibus
subjectis applicata, non tamen de iisdem disserere proposuimus; pro
diversitate enim subjectorum variantur etiam rationes, quae rebus ipsis
applicantur.

[The end of knowledge is virtue, insofar as it directs not only the
intellect but also the will to particular actions; and although this rule
is applied to different subject matters of sciences, we have not proposed
to discuss the same subjects; for the diversity of subjects varies the
very reasons that apply to the things themselves.]

— end of AT X 360 line 14 —
